topic.angle: Why a higher bracket never means a smaller paycheck from the extra earnings

card.title: A raise can't shrink your pay

body.claim: Moving into a higher US tax bracket doesn't tax all your income at the higher rate.
body.why: Income is taxed in layers called brackets, and only the part that falls inside the new bracket gets the higher rate. For a single filer in 2025, the 12% layer ends at $48,475, so each dollar above that is taxed at 22% while every earlier dollar keeps its old rate. That leaves 78 cents of each extra dollar after federal income tax.

probes.question: A single filer's taxable income goes from $48,000 to $49,000 (2025 rates). What rate applies to the dollars above $48,475?
True or false: when your income reaches a higher tax bracket, the higher rate applies to all of your income.
